summary: Defines a way for SIP presence subscribers to receive only the parts of a presence document that changed, instead of the full document each time. By default, any small change causes the whole presence document to be delivered again. This extension reduces that traffic, which helps on slow or constrained networks.

eli5.summary: When a friend changes only their mood on a chat app, you do not need their whole profile again. This tells the server to send you just the new mood, which saves data.

subtitle: A SIP extension that lets presence servers send only what changed instead of the whole presence document every time.

tldr.problem: By default, when any part of a person's presence document changes, even one element, the server delivers a new document with the full set of elements. That wastes bandwidth, especially on slow, high-latency links.
tldr.mechanism: A watcher adds application/pidf-diff+xml to the Accept header of its SUBSCRIBE request. The presence agent then sends a full document first, followed by numbered NOTIFY requests that carry only the added, removed and replaced parts.
tldr.outcome: Less presence data crosses the network. RFC 5263 is a Proposed Standard that has been updated by RFC 8996.

facts.label: Version step
facts.value: Incremented by one per partial notification

today: RFC 5263 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2008 and has been updated by RFC 8996. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: The Problem with Full Presence Documents
sections.content:
The SIP presence event package lets watchers subscribe to the presence information of presentities. That information is a document made of elements called presence tuples, and it can be large. In the baseline behavior, the presence agent (PA) always delivers all the presence data authorized for that watcher, regardless of what changed since the last notification.

The RFC points out that sending the complete document over low bandwidth and high latency links, when only part has changed, can degrade the presence service and give the watcher a bad impression of it. RFC 5263 therefore defines a partial notification approach in which the server sends only the parts that changed since the previous notifications.
sections.eli5: Imagine a friend repainting one wall and mailing you a photo of the entire house each time. This extension says to just send a photo of the wall.

sections.title: How Partial Notification Works
sections.content:
In normal operation a watcher sends a SIP SUBSCRIBE to the presentity, optionally with an Accept header naming content types. The PA answers with NOTIFY requests carrying a PIDF document with the full state.

For partial notification, the watcher lists both application/pidf+xml and application/pidf-diff+xml in its Accept header. If the PA sees the second type, it can decide to use the mechanism and sets the Content-Type of its NOTIFY requests to application/pidf-diff+xml. The first NOTIFY with presence information carries a full document, and later ones can carry partial documents.

The mechanism builds on the presence event package (RFC 3856) and on the partial presence format defined in RFC 5262. Unless this RFC says otherwise, regular watcher and PA behavior applies.
sections.eli5: The watcher says, 'I can read either the whole story or just the changes.' The server, if it agrees, sends the whole story once and then only changes.

sections.title: What the Watcher Must Do
sections.content:
A watcher that wants partial notifications MUST include an Accept header whose value contains application/pidf-diff+xml in addition to application/pidf+xml. It MAY add a q parameter to each value to show its relative preference. Entities that support the extension MUST support the application/pidf-diff+xml content type.

On receiving the first such document, the watcher MUST initialize a version counter for the subscription to the document's version value and store the full document as its local copy. For each later document it compares versions:

  • A version equal to or lower than the local counter is treated as a PA failure, and the watcher SHOULD discard the document.
  • A pidf-full root replaces the local copy and sets the counter to the document's version.
  • A pidf-diff root whose version is exactly one higher is applied to the local copy, and the counter is incremented by one.
  • A pidf-diff root whose version is higher by more than one means one or more NOTIFYs were lost. The watcher SHOULD refresh the subscription to get a full document, or terminate it.

If processing a document fails, the watcher SHOULD renew the subscription. It MAY also fall back to normal presence by leaving the diff type out of a new SUBSCRIBE. If the PA switches content types mid-subscription, the watcher MUST discard previously received presence information for that presentity but keep its version counter, since the count continues if the PA switches back.
sections.eli5: The watcher keeps a numbered copy of the friend's status. Each update says 'this is number 5,' so if number 4 never showed up, the watcher knows something is missing and asks for a fresh copy.

sections.title: What the Presence Agent Must Do
sections.content:
The PA compares the watcher's Accept values with what it supports and decides which to use. If the watcher gave q preferences, the PA SHOULD follow them unless its local policy says otherwise.

Once the subscription is accepted, the PA MUST deliver the full state in the first partial notification, in a document with a <pidf-full> root element. It MUST include a version attribute, starting at one (1) for the first partial notification of a subscription and incremented by one for each following one. The counter is reset only when the subscription ends, not when it is refreshed.

Later documents SHOULD include only what changed. What counts as a change is up to the PA's local policy. Added information goes in <add> elements, removed information in <remove> and changed information in <replace>. The PA MUST NOT send another partial NOTIFY for the same Request-URI until it has a final response to the previous one or that request has timed out.

When the PA receives a refresh or termination SUBSCRIBE, it SHOULD send a NOTIFY with the full presence document. If it switches from some other content type to the diff type mid-subscription, the first partial notification MUST again be a full <pidf-full> document.
sections.eli5: The server numbers every update 1, 2, 3 and so on, sends the whole picture first, and then sends only small patches. It waits for the watcher to say 'got it' before sending the next patch.

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
The RFC walks through a full exchange. The watcher sends a SUBSCRIBE with Accept: application/pidf+xml;q=0.3, application/pidf-diff+xml;q=1 and Expires: 3600. The PA replies 200 OK and, because of the q values, chooses partial notifications. Its first NOTIFY carries a pidf-full document with version="1".

Later the presentity's presence changes and the PA sends a second NOTIFY with a pidf-diff document with version="2". It adds a new tuple, replaces a status value and a contact priority, and removes one activity element. Each NOTIFY is acknowledged with 200 OK.
sections.eli5: First the watcher gets the full picture marked number 1. Then, when something changes, it gets a short note marked number 2 saying 'add this, change that, remove this one.'

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The extension relies on the presence event package, and all security considerations from that package apply unchanged, including confidentiality, integrity and authenticity, replay prevention and denial-of-service concerns.

Partial notifications can reveal what has changed, which may help an eavesdropper see what kind of changes are happening, but the RFC notes the same can be learned with baseline PIDF. A third party could inject a partial NOTIFY that makes the watcher think it missed one and request a new full document, which the RFC considers no worse than injecting a NOTIFY with Subscription-State: terminated.

The RFC says TLS is RECOMMENDED between elements for hop-by-hop confidentiality, and that S/MIME MAY be used for integrity and authenticity of SUBSCRIBE and NOTIFY requests.
sections.eli5: Sending only changes shows what changed, but a snooper could already learn that from full updates. The usual protections, like encrypted connections, still apply.
